stem_book: Fill in the blank with appropriate term. (i) The degree of dissociation is defined as the fraction of a mole of reactant that has ______ at equilibrium. (ii) The ______, represented as Q, is calculated in the same way as the equilibrium constant, but from concentrations at any point in time, not necessarily at equilibrium. (iii) If Qc > Kc, the reaction will proceed in the ______ direction to reach equilibrium. (iv) The relationship between the equilibrium constant and Gibbs free energy is given by the equation: ΔG = −RT ln ______. (v) If the reaction is exergonic (ΔG < 0), the reaction proceeds in the ______ direction.
key: (i) dissociated (ii) reaction quotient (iii) reverse (backward) (iv) K (v) forward
derived: (i) dissociated (ii) reaction quotient (iii) reverse (backward) (iv) K (v) forward
correct_answer: (i) dissociated (ii) reaction quotient (iii) reverse (backward) (iv) K (v) forward
reason: Five-part fill-in-the-blanks recap with separate answers; manifest split it into 5 entries sharing one code. Print writes ΔG = −RT ln K (should be ΔG° = −RT ln K).
work: Qc > Kc → excess products → reverse; ΔG° = −RT ln K; ΔG < 0 → forward
